questions.stem:
On January 1, Year 1, Kessler Co. grants 12,000 cash-settled stock appreciation rights (SARs) to its employees. The SARs cliff-vest at the end of Year 3, and the grant-date fair value is $8 per SAR. Kessler expects all of the SARs to vest. The fair value of each SAR at each subsequent reporting date is as follows.

Reporting date | Fair value per SAR
December 31, Year 1 | $9
December 31, Year 2 | $13
December 31, Year 3 | $11

What amount of compensation expense should Kessler recognize for Year 2?
questions.explanation: A cash-settled SAR is a liability-classified award. The liability is remeasured to fair value at every reporting date, and the cumulative cost recognized equals the current fair value multiplied by the portion of the requisite service period completed. At the end of Year 1 the cumulative cost is 12,000 x $9 x 1/3 = $36,000. At the end of Year 2 the cumulative cost is 12,000 x $13 x 2/3 = $104,000. Year 2 expense is therefore $104,000 - $36,000 = $68,000. The $104,000 amount is the cumulative liability balance, not the expense for the year. The $52,000 amount applies only one year of service (12,000 x $13 x 1/3) instead of the two years completed. The $32,000 amount freezes the measurement at the $8 grant-date fair value, which is the treatment for equity-classified awards, not liability awards.
questions.explanationJa: 現金決済型SARは負債分類の報酬であり、各報告日ごとに公正価値へ再測定する。累積費用は「期末公正価値 × 経過した勤務期間の割合」で計算する。Year 1末の累積費用は 12,000 × $9 × 1/3 = $36,000。Year 2末の累積費用は 12,000 × $13 × 2/3 = $104,000。したがって Year 2 の費用は $104,000 − $36,000 = $68,000 となる。$104,000 は累積の負債残高であって当期費用ではない。$52,000 は経過済みの2年ではなく1年分（12,000 × $13 × 1/3）しか計上していない誤り。$32,000 は測定を付与日公正価値 $8 に固定したもので、これは資本分類の処理であり負債分類には当てはまらない。

questions.stem:
On January 1, Year 1, Marek Corp. grants 15,000 cash-settled stock appreciation rights (SARs) that cliff-vest at the end of Year 4. All of the SARs are expected to vest. The fair value of each SAR at each reporting date is as follows.

Reporting date | Fair value per SAR
December 31, Year 1 | $6
December 31, Year 2 | $10
December 31, Year 3 | $9
December 31, Year 4 | $14

What amount should Marek report as the liability for these SARs in its December 31, Year 3 balance sheet?
questions.explanation: For a liability-classified award, the liability at each reporting date equals the current fair value of the award multiplied by the fraction of the requisite service period that has elapsed. At December 31, Year 3, three of the four years of service are complete and the current fair value is $9 per SAR: 15,000 x $9 x 3/4 = $101,250. The $135,000 amount recognizes the full fair value of all 15,000 SARs without prorating for the unfinished service period. The $112,500 amount uses the stale $10 fair value from the prior reporting date instead of remeasuring to the $9 current fair value. The $67,500 amount prorates for only two of the four years of service.
questions.explanationJa: 負債分類の報酬では、各報告日の負債は「期末時点の公正価値 × 経過した必要勤務期間の割合」で測定する。Year 3末は4年のうち3年が経過し、公正価値は1個あたり $9 なので、15,000 × $9 × 3/4 = $101,250 となる。$135,000 は未経過の勤務期間について按分せず全額を計上した誤り。$112,500 は再測定を行わず前期末の $10 をそのまま使っている。$67,500 は4年のうち2年分しか按分していない。

questions.subtopic: Cash-Settled SAR — Partial Exercise and Settlement
questions.stem: At December 31, Year 3, Rowan Inc. has 20,000 fully vested cash-settled stock appreciation rights (SARs) outstanding, and the related liability is carried at $160,000 ($8 per SAR). On September 1, Year 4, employees exercise 12,000 of the SARs and Rowan pays cash based on an intrinsic value of $11 per SAR. At December 31, Year 4, the fair value of the remaining 8,000 SARs is $9 per SAR. What total amount of compensation expense should Rowan recognize for Year 4?
questions.explanation: A liability award continues to be remeasured after vesting until it is settled, and every change in the liability runs through compensation expense. The 12,000 SARs exercised were carried at 12,000 x $8 = $96,000 and were settled for 12,000 x $11 = $132,000, producing $36,000 of expense. The 8,000 SARs still outstanding were carried at 8,000 x $8 = $64,000 and are remeasured to 8,000 x $9 = $72,000, producing $8,000 of expense. Total Year 4 expense is $36,000 + $8,000 = $44,000. The $36,000 amount ignores the remeasurement of the unexercised SARs, and the $8,000 amount ignores the settlement of the exercised SARs. The $132,000 amount is the cash paid, most of which relieves the liability already recorded rather than creating expense.
questions.explanationJa: 負債分類の報酬は権利確定後も決済まで再測定を続け、負債の変動はすべて報酬費用として認識する。行使された12,000個は 12,000 × $8 = $96,000 で計上されていたが 12,000 × $11 = $132,000 で決済されたため、差額 $36,000 が費用となる。未行使の8,000個は 8,000 × $8 = $64,000 から 8,000 × $9 = $72,000 へ再測定され、$8,000 の費用が生じる。Year 4 の費用合計は $36,000 + $8,000 = $44,000。$36,000 は未行使分の再測定を無視し、$8,000 は行使分の決済差額を無視している。$132,000 は支払現金の総額で、その大部分は既に計上済みの負債の取り崩しであり費用ではない。

questions.subtopic: Cash-Settled SAR — Decline in Fair Value
questions.stem:
On January 1, Year 1, Ashland Co. grants 8,000 cash-settled stock appreciation rights (SARs) that cliff-vest at the end of Year 4. All of the SARs are expected to vest. The fair value of each SAR at each reporting date is as follows.

Reporting date | Fair value per SAR
December 31, Year 1 | $12
December 31, Year 2 | $15
December 31, Year 3 | $9
December 31, Year 4 | $13

What amount should Ashland recognize in Year 3 with respect to these SARs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $18,000 of compensation expense

choices.label: B
choices.text: A $6,000 credit that reduces compensation expense

choices.label: C
choices.text: $54,000 of compensation expense

choices.label: D
choices.text: No amount, because cumulative expense on a liability award is never reduced

questions.explanation: Cumulative cost on a liability award is always trued up to the current fair value times the elapsed service fraction, so a decline in fair value produces a credit. At the end of Year 2 the cumulative cost is 8,000 x $15 x 2/4 = $60,000. At the end of Year 3 the cumulative cost is 8,000 x $9 x 3/4 = $54,000. Because the required cumulative balance fell from $60,000 to $54,000, Ashland records a $6,000 credit to compensation expense. The $54,000 amount is the cumulative balance, not the Year 3 charge. The $18,000 amount applies only a single year of service (8,000 x $9 x 1/4). Treating the cumulative expense as irreversible is the rule for equity-classified awards that fail a market condition, not for liability awards, whose measurement continues through settlement.
questions.explanationJa: 負債分類の報酬は常に「期末公正価値 × 経過勤務割合」へ累積費用を修正するため、公正価値が下落すれば貸方（費用の戻し）が生じる。Year 2末の累積費用は 8,000 × $15 × 2/4 = $60,000、Year 3末は 8,000 × $9 × 3/4 = $54,000。必要な累積残高が $60,000 から $54,000 へ減少したため、$6,000 を報酬費用の減額として計上する。$54,000 は累積残高であって当期の計上額ではない。$18,000 は1年分（8,000 × $9 × 1/4）しか按分していない。累積費用が戻らないのは市場条件を満たさなかった資本分類の報酬の話であり、決済まで再測定を続ける負債分類には当てはまらない。

questions.stem: Under ASC 718, after a cash-settled stock appreciation right has fully vested but has not yet been exercised, how should the entity account for subsequent changes in the fair value of the award?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continue to remeasure the liability to fair value at each reporting date, with the change recognized in compensation cost in current earnings

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stop remeasuring the award, because the requisite service period has ended and the total compensation cost is fixed at the vesting-date amount

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue to remeasure the award, but record the change as an adjustment of additional paid-in capital rather than in earnings

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continue to remeasure the award, but recognize the change in other comprehensive income until the right is exercised

questions.explanation: A liability-classified share-based payment is remeasured to fair value at every reporting date until the award is settled, not merely until it vests. Once vesting is complete the entire change in fair value is recognized immediately in compensation cost, because there is no remaining service period over which to attribute it. Freezing the measurement at the vesting date is the pattern for equity-classified awards, which are measured once at grant date and never remeasured. Routing the change to additional paid-in capital would treat the obligation as equity even though the entity must deliver cash, and there is no basis under ASC 718 for deferring the remeasurement in other comprehensive income.
questions.explanationJa: 負債分類の株式報酬は権利確定時点までではなく決済されるまで、各報告日ごとに公正価値へ再測定する。権利確定後は按分すべき残存勤務期間がないため、公正価値の変動は全額がただちに報酬費用として認識される。権利確定日で測定を止めるのは、付与日に一度だけ測定してその後再測定しない資本分類の報酬の扱いである。変動を資本剰余金（APIC）で処理するのは、現金を支払う義務があるにもかかわらず資本として扱うことになり誤り。またASC 718 に再測定差額をその他の包括利益で繰り延べる規定はない。

questions.subtopic: Liability Award — Total Cost Through Expiration
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Bellamy Corp. grants 6,000 cash-settled stock appreciation rights (SARs) to employees. The grant-date fair value is $10 per SAR and the SARs cliff-vest at the end of Year 2. During Year 3, employees exercise 4,000 of the SARs and Bellamy pays cash of $11 per SAR. The remaining 2,000 SARs are never exercised and expire worthless at the end of Year 4 because the share price stays below the grant-date price. What total compensation cost does Bellamy recognize over the entire life of this award?
questions.explanation: Because a liability award is remeasured through settlement, the total compensation cost recognized over the life of the award equals the cash ultimately paid. Bellamy pays 4,000 x $11 = $44,000 and pays nothing for the 2,000 SARs that expire, so any liability previously accrued for those units is reversed against compensation cost. Total cost is therefore $44,000. The $60,000 amount uses the $10 grant-date fair value for all 6,000 SARs, which would be correct only for an equity-classified award. The $66,000 amount applies the $11 settlement value to all 6,000 SARs, including the units that were never exercised and cost the company nothing. The $40,000 amount mixes the 4,000 units actually settled with the grant-date fair value instead of the amount actually paid.
questions.explanationJa: 負債分類の報酬は決済まで再測定されるため、全期間で認識する報酬費用の総額は最終的に支払った現金と一致する。Bellamy は 4,000 × $11 = $44,000 を支払い、失効した2,000個には何も支払わないので、それらについて過去に計上した負債は報酬費用の戻しとして取り消される。したがって費用総額は $44,000。$60,000 は全6,000個に付与日公正価値 $10 を用いたもので、これは資本分類の報酬にのみ当てはまる。$66,000 は一度も行使されず支出が生じなかった分にも決済単価 $11 を掛けている。$40,000 は実際に決済した4,000個に、支払額ではなく付与日公正価値を掛けている。

questions.subtopic: Classification — Fixed Monetary Amount in Variable Shares
questions.stem: Delvano Inc. grants an award to a key executive that obligates Delvano to deliver, at the end of a three-year service period, a number of its own common shares with a total fair value equal to $150,000 on the settlement date. The number of shares to be issued will be whatever is necessary to equal that fixed monetary amount. How should Delvano classify and measure this award under ASC 718?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As equity, measured once at the grant-date fair value of the shares expected to be issued

choices.label: B
choices.text: As a liability, remeasured at fair value at each reporting date until settlement

choices.label: C
choices.text: As equity, with the number of shares and the related cost trued up to the settlement-date share price

choices.label: D
choices.text: As a liability only if Delvano does not have enough authorized but unissued shares to satisfy the award

questions.explanation: An award that requires the entity to transfer a variable number of its own shares whose total value is fixed at a monetary amount conveys none of the risks and rewards of share ownership to the holder, so ASC 718 classifies it as a liability even though it is settled in shares rather than cash. The liability is remeasured to fair value at each reporting date, with the cost attributed over the three-year service period. Treating the award as equity measured at grant date would apply the rule for awards settled in a fixed number of shares. Truing up an equity-classified award to the settlement-date price contradicts the principle that equity awards are never remeasured after grant. The availability of authorized shares affects whether an entity can achieve share settlement of other awards, but it does not drive classification here, where the fixed monetary amount is itself determinative.
questions.explanationJa: 決済額が固定の金額で、引き渡す自社株式の数が変動する報酬は、保有者に株主としてのリスクとリターンを与えないため、株式で決済されるにもかかわらずASC 718 上は負債に分類される。負債は各報告日ごとに公正価値へ再測定し、費用は3年の勤務期間にわたって按分する。付与日測定の資本分類とするのは、固定株数で決済される報酬に対する扱いである。資本分類のまま決済日株価へ修正するという処理は、資本分類の報酬は付与後に再測定しないという原則に反する。授権未発行株式の有無は他の報酬の株式決済可能性に影響することはあるが、ここでは決済額が固定金額であること自体が分類を決めるため関係しない。

questions.stem: Corliss Co., a nonpublic entity, grants shares of its common stock to employees that vest after two years of service. Each of the following repurchase features is attached to a separate grant. Which feature causes the related award to be classified as a liability rather than as equity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The employee may put the shares back to Corliss at their fair value, but only after holding the vested shares for more than six months

choices.label: B
choices.text: Corliss has a right of first refusal to buy the shares at fair value if the employee decides to sell them to a third party

choices.label: C
choices.text: The shares carry no repurchase feature but are subject to a transfer restriction until Corliss completes an initial public offering

choices.label: D
choices.text: The employee may put the shares back to Corliss at a formula price based on book value, exercisable immediately upon vesting

questions.explanation: A repurchase feature causes liability classification when it prevents the employee from bearing the risks and rewards of share ownership for a reasonable period. A put exercisable immediately upon vesting at a book-value formula price fails on both counts: the holder is never exposed to changes in the fair value of the shares, so the arrangement is in substance an obligation to pay cash. A put at fair value that cannot be exercised until the shares have been held for more than six months after vesting leaves the employee exposed to share price changes for a reasonable period and preserves equity classification. A right of first refusal at fair value does not transfer value away from the holder and does not affect classification. A transfer restriction that lapses on an initial public offering affects the measurement of fair value through a discount for lack of marketability, but it does not convert the award into a liability.
questions.explanationJa: 買戻条項が負債分類を招くのは、従業員が相当期間にわたり株主としてのリスクとリターンを負わない場合である。権利確定と同時に行使でき、かつ簿価に基づく算式価格で買い戻される条項は両方の点で失格であり、保有者は株価変動に一切さらされないため、実質的に現金支払義務となる。権利確定後6か月超保有しないと行使できない公正価値によるプット条項は、相当期間の株価変動リスクを従業員に負わせるため資本分類が維持される。公正価値での先買権は保有者から価値を移転しないので分類に影響しない。IPOまでの譲渡制限は市場性欠如ディスカウントとして公正価値の測定に影響するが、報酬を負債に変えるものではない。

questions.stem: Vantor Co. grants restricted stock units that will be settled by delivering a fixed number of Vantor common shares at the end of a four-year service period. The award agreement provides that if a change in control of Vantor occurs before settlement, the units will instead be settled in cash. At the current reporting date, a change in control is not considered probable. How should Vantor classify the award at the current reporting date?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As equity, with reclassification to a liability at the date the change in control becomes probable

choices.label: B
choices.text: As a liability from the grant date, because a cash settlement feature exists in the award terms

choices.label: C
choices.text: As equity for the entire life of the award, because the terms at grant date specify settlement in a fixed number of shares

choices.label: D
choices.text: Split between equity and liability in proportion to the estimated likelihood of the change in control occurring

questions.explanation: When cash settlement of an otherwise share-settled award depends on a contingent event that is outside the employee's control, classification follows the probability of that event. While the contingent event is not probable, the award stays in equity and is measured at its grant-date fair value. If and when the change in control becomes probable, the award is reclassified as a liability and remeasured to fair value at that date, with the difference recorded against equity. Classifying the award as a liability from grant date would ignore the probability assessment that the standard requires. Permanently classifying it as equity ignores that the entity can be forced to pay cash once the contingency becomes probable. ASC 718 does not permit an award to be split between equity and liability based on the likelihood of the contingency.
questions.explanationJa: 本来は株式決済である報酬について、現金決済が従業員の支配の及ばない条件付事象に依存する場合、分類はその事象の発生可能性に従う。条件付事象が probable でない間は資本分類のままで、付与日公正価値で測定する。支配権の異動が probable となった時点で負債へ振り替え、その日の公正価値へ再測定し、差額は資本で調整する。付与日から負債とする処理は、基準が求める発生可能性の判定を無視している。恒久的に資本分類とする処理は、条件が probable になれば現金支払を強制されうる点を無視している。ASC 718 は発生確率に応じて資本と負債に按分することを認めていない。

questions.subtopic: Modification — Incremental Fair Value in Year of Repricing
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Norbeck Co. grants 12,000 equity-classified stock options with a grant-date fair value of $9 per option. The options cliff-vest at the end of Year 3. On January 1, Year 2, with the options deeply underwater, Norbeck reduces the exercise price. Immediately before the repricing each option has a fair value of $4; immediately after the repricing each option has a fair value of $7. The vesting date is unchanged and all of the options are expected to vest. What amount of compensation expense should Norbeck recognize for Year 2?
questions.explanation: A modification does not disturb the original grant-date compensation cost, which continues to be recognized over the remaining service period; the entity adds only the incremental fair value created by the modification. The original cost is 12,000 x $9 = $108,000 spread over three years, or $36,000 per year. The incremental fair value is ($7 - $4) x 12,000 = $36,000, recognized over the two years remaining to the vesting date, or $18,000 per year. Year 2 expense is $36,000 + $18,000 = $54,000. The $36,000 amount recognizes only the original cost and ignores the incremental value entirely. The $72,000 amount charges the whole $36,000 of incremental value to Year 2 instead of spreading it over the remaining service period. The $28,000 amount remeasures the entire award at the $7 post-modification fair value (12,000 x $7 divided by 3 years), which would improperly replace the original grant-date measurement.
questions.explanationJa: 条件変更を行っても当初の付与日報酬費用は消えず、残存勤務期間にわたり引き続き認識する。加算するのは条件変更で生じた増分公正価値だけである。当初費用は 12,000 × $9 = $108,000 を3年で按分し年 $36,000。増分公正価値は（$7 − $4）× 12,000 = $36,000 で、権利確定日まで残る2年で按分し年 $18,000。したがって Year 2 の費用は $36,000 + $18,000 = $54,000。$36,000 は増分を完全に無視している。$72,000 は増分 $36,000 を残存期間で按分せず Year 2 に全額計上している。$28,000 は報酬全体を変更後公正価値 $7 で測り直し（12,000 × $7 ÷ 3年）ており、当初の付与日測定を置き換えてしまう誤りである。

questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Delaney Corp. grants 8,000 equity-classified stock options with a grant-date fair value of $12 per option that cliff-vest at the end of Year 3. On December 31, Year 1, Delaney modifies the awards by increasing the exercise price. Immediately before the modification each option has a fair value of $10; immediately after the modification each option has a fair value of $6. All of the employees continue in service and all of the options ultimately vest. What total compensation cost should Delaney recognize over the three-year vesting period?
questions.explanation: Incremental compensation cost from a modification is the excess of the fair value of the modified award over the fair value of the original award immediately before the modification, and that excess cannot be negative. Here the fair value fell from $10 to $6, so the incremental cost is zero. The original grant-date cost of 8,000 x $12 = $96,000 is still recognized in full because the employees render the requisite service and the awards vest. The $48,000 amount remeasures the award at the $6 post-modification fair value, and the $80,000 amount uses the $10 pre-modification fair value; neither may replace the grant-date measurement of an equity award. The $64,000 amount subtracts the $32,000 decline in value from the original cost, which would let a modification reduce compensation cost below the grant-date amount.
questions.explanationJa: 条件変更による増分報酬費用は「変更後の公正価値 − 変更直前の公正価値」であり、この差額がマイナスになることはない。本問では公正価値が $10 から $6 へ下落したため増分費用はゼロである。従業員は必要勤務を提供し権利も確定するので、当初の付与日費用 8,000 × $12 = $96,000 は全額そのまま認識される。$48,000 は変更後公正価値 $6 で、$80,000 は変更直前の $10 で測り直したものだが、いずれも資本分類の報酬の付与日測定を置き換えることはできない。$64,000 は価値下落分 $32,000 を当初費用から差し引いており、条件変更によって報酬費用が付与日の金額を下回ることを認めてしまう誤りである。

questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Yardley Inc. grants 40,000 restricted stock units with a grant-date fair value of $15 per unit that cliff-vest at the end of Year 4. Yardley elects to estimate forfeitures and initially expects 10% of the units to be forfeited. Employee turnover is lower than anticipated, and at the end of Year 3 Yardley revises its estimate so that only 4% of the units are now expected to be forfeited. What amount of compensation expense should Yardley recognize for Year 3?
questions.explanation: A change in the estimated forfeiture rate is a change in accounting estimate recognized through a cumulative catch-up in the period of the change. Under the original 10% estimate, 36,000 units x $15 = $540,000 of total cost was being spread over four years, so Years 1 and 2 each recorded $135,000 and cumulative expense reached $270,000. The revised 4% estimate gives total cost of 38,400 units x $15 = $576,000, and three of four years are complete, so cumulative expense must be $576,000 x 3/4 = $432,000. Year 3 expense is $432,000 - $270,000 = $162,000. The $432,000 amount is the required cumulative balance rather than the Year 3 charge. The $144,000 amount ($576,000 divided by four years) applies the new estimate prospectively only and omits the catch-up for Years 1 and 2. The $135,000 amount ignores the revision entirely.
questions.explanationJa: 失効見積率の変更は会計上の見積りの変更であり、変更した期に累積差額を一括して調整（キャッチアップ）する。当初の10%見積りでは総費用 36,000個 × $15 = $540,000 を4年で按分し、Year 1・Year 2 は各 $135,000、累積 $270,000 が計上済みである。改訂後の4%見積りでは総費用が 38,400個 × $15 = $576,000 となり、4年のうち3年が経過しているので累積費用は $576,000 × 3/4 = $432,000 でなければならない。よって Year 3 の費用は $432,000 − $270,000 = $162,000。$432,000 はあるべき累積残高であって当期費用ではない。$144,000（$576,000 ÷ 4年）は新見積りを将来に向かってのみ適用し、Year 1・Year 2 分のキャッチアップを落としている。$135,000 は見積り変更自体を反映していない。

questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Hollis Co. grants 30,000 stock options with a grant-date fair value of $8 per option that cliff-vest at the end of Year 3. Hollis elects to estimate forfeitures and initially expects that 5% of the options will be forfeited. Turnover accelerates during Year 2, and at the end of Year 2 Hollis revises its estimate so that 20% of the options are now expected to be forfeited. What amount of compensation expense should Hollis recognize for Year 2?
questions.explanation: Under the original 5% forfeiture estimate, total cost was 28,500 options x $8 = $228,000 over three years, so Year 1 expense was $76,000. The revision to a 20% forfeiture rate lowers total expected cost to 24,000 options x $8 = $192,000, and two of the three years are complete, so cumulative expense must be $192,000 x 2/3 = $128,000. Year 2 expense is $128,000 - $76,000 = $52,000, which is less than a normal year because the catch-up for Year 1's overstatement is absorbed in the current period. The $128,000 amount is the required cumulative balance, not the Year 2 charge. The $64,000 amount ($192,000 divided by three years) applies the revised estimate as if it had been used since inception without computing the catch-up. The $76,000 amount simply repeats Year 1 and ignores the revision.
questions.explanationJa: 当初の失効率5%では総費用が 28,500個 × $8 = $228,000 で3年按分のため Year 1 の費用は $76,000 であった。失効率を20%へ改訂すると総費用は 24,000個 × $8 = $192,000 となり、3年のうち2年が経過しているので累積費用は $192,000 × 2/3 = $128,000 でなければならない。したがって Year 2 の費用は $128,000 − $76,000 = $52,000 となり、Year 1 の過大計上分のキャッチアップを当期で吸収するため通常の年より小さくなる。$128,000 はあるべき累積残高であって当期費用ではない。$64,000（$192,000 ÷ 3年）はキャッチアップを計算せず、改訂後の見積りを当初から使っていたかのように単純按分したもの。$76,000 は Year 1 と同額を置いただけで見積り変更を反映していない。

questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Calloway Co. grants 25,000 equity-classified stock options with a grant-date fair value of $10 per option. The options vest at the end of Year 4 only if Calloway achieves a specified cumulative revenue target over the four-year period. At December 31, Year 1, achievement of the target is not considered probable. During Year 2, sales improve sharply and at December 31, Year 2 achievement of the target is considered probable. What amount of compensation expense should Calloway recognize for Year 2?
questions.explanation: Compensation cost for an award with a performance condition is recognized only when achievement of the condition is probable, and the assessment is revisited each reporting period. No cost was recognized in Year 1 because the target was not probable. Once the target becomes probable in Year 2, the cumulative expense must equal the total grant-date cost multiplied by the elapsed portion of the service period: 25,000 x $10 = $250,000, multiplied by 2/4, equals $125,000. Because nothing was recognized in Year 1, the full $125,000 is recorded in Year 2 as a catch-up. The $62,500 amount recognizes only one year of the four-year period and ignores the Year 1 catch-up. The $250,000 amount is the total cost of the award, which is attributed over the full four years rather than recognized when the condition becomes probable. Recognizing nothing would be correct only if the target remained improbable.
questions.explanationJa: 業績条件付きの報酬費用は、条件の達成が probable と判断された場合にのみ認識し、その判定は各報告期間ごとに見直す。Year 1 は目標達成が probable でなかったため費用はゼロ。Year 2 に probable となった時点で、累積費用は「付与日総費用 × 経過した勤務期間の割合」とならねばならず、25,000 × $10 = $250,000 に 2/4 を掛けて $125,000 となる。Year 1 に何も計上していないため、$125,000 全額がキャッチアップとして Year 2 に計上される。$62,500 は4年のうち1年分しか認識せず Year 1 のキャッチアップを落としている。$250,000 は報酬の総費用であり、4年にわたって按分されるべきものである。費用ゼロとなるのは目標が引き続き probable でない場合に限られる。

questions.subtopic: Performance Condition on a Liability Award — Reversal
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Straiton Co. grants 6,000 cash-settled performance units to executives. The units vest at the end of Year 3 only if a cumulative EBITDA target is achieved. At December 31, Year 1, achievement of the target is considered probable and the fair value of each unit is $20. At December 31, Year 2, the fair value of each unit has risen to $26, but a major customer loss makes achievement of the EBITDA target no longer probable. What amount should Straiton recognize in Year 2 with respect to these units?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A $40,000 credit that reverses previously recognized compensation cost

choices.label: C
choices.text: $64,000 of compensation expense

choices.label: D
choices.text: $104,000 of compensation expense

questions.explanation: These units are liability-classified because they are settled in cash, but they also carry a performance condition, and no cost is recognized for an award whose performance condition is not expected to be satisfied. In Year 1 the target was probable, so Straiton recognized 6,000 x $20 x 1/3 = $40,000. Once the target is no longer probable in Year 2, the required cumulative cost is zero and the previously recorded liability of $40,000 is reversed, producing a $40,000 credit to compensation cost. The $64,000 amount is the Year 2 expense that would have been recorded had the target remained probable ($104,000 cumulative less $40,000 already recognized), and $104,000 is that cumulative amount (6,000 x $26 x 2/3). Recognizing nothing would leave the $40,000 liability on the books even though no payment is expected. Note that the outcome differs from a market condition, for which recognized cost is never reversed.
questions.explanationJa: この報酬単位は現金決済のため負債分類であるが、同時に業績条件を伴っており、達成が見込まれない業績条件付き報酬については費用を認識しない。Year 1 は目標が probable だったため 6,000 × $20 × 1/3 = $40,000 を計上した。Year 2 に目標が probable でなくなった時点であるべき累積費用はゼロとなり、計上済みの負債 $40,000 を取り消して $40,000 を報酬費用の貸方に計上する。$64,000 は目標が probable のままだった場合の Year 2 費用（累積 $104,000 − 計上済み $40,000）であり、$104,000 はその累積額（6,000 × $26 × 2/3）である。何も認識しなければ、支払が見込まれないのに $40,000 の負債が残ってしまう。認識済み費用が決して戻らない市場条件とは結論が異なる点に注意する。

questions.subtopic: Market Condition — Effect on Grant-Date Fair Value
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Ormsby Inc. grants two separate equity-classified option awards, each covering 10,000 shares and each requiring three years of service. Award X has a service condition only, and its grant-date fair value is $12 per option. Award Y has the same terms except that the options also vest only if Ormsby's share price reaches $70; its grant-date fair value is $8 per option. Employees holding Award Y render the full three years of service, but the share price never reaches $70 and the Award Y options never vest. What total compensation cost should Ormsby recognize for Award Y?
questions.explanation: A market condition is reflected in the measurement of the award's grant-date fair value rather than in the number of awards expected to vest, which is why Award Y is valued at $8 per option instead of the $12 per option of the otherwise identical Award X. Once that lower fair value has been established, cost is recognized as long as the requisite service is rendered, and it is not reversed if the market condition is never satisfied. Total cost for Award Y is 10,000 x $8 = $80,000. Recognizing nothing applies the reversal rule for performance and service conditions, which does not extend to market conditions. The $120,000 amount uses the $12 fair value of the award that has no market condition, double counting a condition already built into the valuation. The $40,000 amount is the $4 per option difference between the two valuations, which is not a measure of compensation cost for either award.
questions.explanationJa: 市場条件は権利確定が見込まれる報酬の個数ではなく、付与日公正価値の測定に織り込まれる。これが、条件以外は同一の Award X が1個あたり $12 であるのに対し Award Y が $8 と評価される理由である。この低い公正価値がいったん決まれば、必要な勤務が提供される限り費用は認識され、市場条件が達成されなくても取り消されない。Award Y の費用総額は 10,000 × $8 = $80,000。費用ゼロとするのは業績条件・勤務条件に対する戻し入れの規則を当てはめたもので、市場条件には及ばない。$120,000 は市場条件のない報酬の公正価値 $12 を用いており、すでに評価に織り込まれた条件を二重に考慮している。$40,000 は両者の評価差額 $4 に相当する金額にすぎず、いずれの報酬費用でもない。
